# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Cerou_2024_amcenestrant"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.13128> (open access; Data S1 holds
  Tables S1-S3 and the Monolix model file)

Cerou 2024 built a joint model of target-lesion tumor size (TS, RECIST 1.1 sum
of longest diameters) and progression-free survival (PFS) for the oral selective
estrogen receptor degrader amcenestrant. The paper reports two complete,
jointly fitted models with the same structure, and both are packaged:

| Model | Data | Role in the paper |
|-------|------|-------------------|
| `Cerou_2024_amcenestrant_ameera12` | AMEERA-1 + AMEERA-2, 75 patients | development model, externally evaluated on AMEERA-3 (Figure 2) |
| `Cerou_2024_amcenestrant` | AMEERA-1 + AMEERA-2 + AMEERA-3, 214 patients | final calibrated model (Table 3 right column, Figures 3-4) |

Structure (Methods and the Data S1 Monolix file):

* Amcenestrant PK: a dose into `depot`, three transit states and a
  two-compartment linear model, all transit steps at rate `KTR`.
* Effect delay: two first-order transit compartments at rate `ke0`, fed by the
  molar plasma concentration (molecular weight 554.48 g/mol); the second drives
  an Imax inhibition with Imax fixed to 1.
* Tumor: resistant cells `R` and treatment-sensitive cells `S`, both with
  proliferation `Kg = Ks / RE` and apoptosis `Ks`; the drug inhibits
  proliferation of the sensitive cells only. `TS = R + S`, `R(0) = pR * TS0`.
* PFS: Weibull baseline hazard `(s / Te) (t / Te)^(s - 1)`, multiplied by a
  covariate factor `E` and by `exp(betaL * dTS/dt)`.

**The PK enters as data.** The authors fed each patient's empirical-Bayes PK
parameters from their amcenestrant population PK model into Monolix as
regressors (`KTR`, `CL`, `V1`, `Q`, `V2`). That population PK model is cited
only as a PAGE 2022 abstract that gives no parameter values, and no amcenestrant
population PK paper has been published (literature check, 2026-11-09). The
packaged models therefore keep the authors' design: the PK parameters are
per-subject covariate columns `KTR_INDIV` (1/day), `CL_INDIV` (L/day),
`VC_INDIV` (L), `Q_INDIV` (L/day) and `VP_INDIV` (L). To simulate, supply
values for these columns.

# Population

The calibration dataset (Table 1, Table 2) has 214 women with ER+/HER2- advanced
breast cancer: AMEERA-1 (non-Japanese, n = 68), AMEERA-2 (Japanese, n = 8) and
the amcenestrant arm of the randomized phase II AMEERA-3 (n = 138). Median age
was 60 years (29-88); 47.2% had liver metastases, 45.3% had metastases in three
or more organs and 74.8% had received a CDK4/6 inhibitor. Doses ranged from 20
to 600 mg once daily (QD) or 300 mg twice daily; 194 patients (91%) received
400 mg QD. 178 patients had measurable target lesions and 36 had non-measurable
disease only. The development dataset is the 75 AMEERA-1 and AMEERA-2 patients
with measurable target lesions and at least one post-treatment measurement.

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Cerou_2024_amcenestrant")()$population)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries its source location as an in-file comment. All
parameter values are from Table 3; the structure is from Methods and the
Data S1 Monolix model.

| Parameter | AMEERA-1-2 (`_ameera12`) | AMEERA-1-2-3 (final) | Source |
|-----------|-----------|-----------|--------|
| `lrbase` (TS0, mm) | 37.67 | 43.17 | Table 3 |
| `e_nmetlt3_rbase` (NMET < 3) | -0.36 | -- | Table 3 |
| `e_nmet1_rbase`, `e_nmet2_rbase` | -- | -0.38, -0.40 | Table 3 |
| `e_lmet_rbase` (LIVMET) | 0.41 | 0.25 | Table 3 |
| `e_premenopausal_rbase` | -- | 0.34 | Table 3 |
| `lks` (Ks, 1/day) | 0.09 fixed | 0.09 fixed | Table 3 |
| `logitre` (RE) | 0.988 | 0.992 | Table 3 |
| `e_albr_re`, `e_lnmet_re`, `e_noprior_cdk46i_re` | 5.77, -0.90, 1.73 | -- | Table 3 |
| `e_ast_re`, `e_lmet_re` | -- | -0.57, -0.78 | Table 3 |
| `limax` (Imax) | 1 fixed | 1 fixed | Methods |
| `lic50` (IC50, umol/L) | 1.83 | 3.74 | Table 3; Results give 1014 and 2073 ng/mL |
| `lke0` (ke0, 1/day) | 0.005 fixed | 0.005 fixed | Table 3; grid search in Data S1 |
| `logitpr` (pR) | 0.714 | 0.660 | Table 3 |

| `lk_haz` (s) | 0.79 | 0.84 | Table 3 |
| `e_tsslope_haz` (betaL, day/mm) | 10.20 | 10.73 | Table 3 |
| `e_alpr_haz` | 0.93 | -- | Table 3 (beta E logtALKN) |
| `e_ast_haz`, `e_lmet_haz` | -- | 0.68, 0.52 | Table 3 |
| omega TS0 / RE / pR / ke0 (SD) | 0.57 / 0.88 / 1.40 / 2.60 | 0.57 / 1.25 / 0.84 / 3.51 | Table 3 (printed x 100) |

Two consistency checks on the transcription:

```{r transcription-checks}
mw <- 554.48
ic50_ngml <- c(dev = 1.83, final = 3.74) * mw
kg <- c(dev = 0.09 / 0.988, final = 0.09 / 0.992)
ic50_ngml
kg
# Results: 'IC50 ... 1014 ng/mL, corresponding to ... 1.83 umol/L' and
# '3.74 umol/L (i.e., 2073 ng/mL)'; 'RE ... translates to kg of 0.091 day-1'.
stopifnot(
  abs(ic50_ngml[["dev"]] - 1014) < 2,
  abs(ic50_ngml[["final"]] - 2073) < 2,
  all(abs(kg - 0.091) < 0.0005)
)
```

# An illustrative amcenestrant PK input

The validation below needs PK parameter values. Because the authors' population
PK model is unpublished, the maintainers built a typical-patient PK input from
published noncompartmental results at 400 mg QD. The structure is the authors'
(depot, three transit states, two compartments). CL/F is fixed to
400 mg / AUCtau at day 22 (39,800 h*ng/mL; Tamura 2023, AMEERA-2, Table 3), and
KTR, V1, Q and V2 were chosen to match the day-22 median tmax (2.97 h),
geometric-mean Cmax (4,880 ng/mL) and a trough of 400 ng/mL, between the
AMEERA-2 mean trough (348 ng/mL, Results text) and the AMEERA-1 geometric-mean
trough at day 22 (466 ng/mL; Bardia 2022). **These values
are not the authors' population PK model.** The TGI and PFS predictions depend
on PK mainly through the average concentration (ke0 = 0.005/day averages away
the daily profile), and the average concentration is set by CL/F, which both
clinical papers report (10.1 and 10.6 L/h).

```{r typical-pk}
typical_pk <- data.frame(
  KTR_INDIV = 52.7, # 1/day
  CL_INDIV = 400 / 39.8 * 24, # L/day: 400 mg / AUCtau 39.8 mg*h/L
  VC_INDIV = 59.3, # L
  Q_INDIV = 64.2, # L/day
  VP_INDIV = 296 # L
)
typical_pk
```

The PK part of the model is checked with PKNCA against the published NCA. The
model is linear, so day-1 exposure cannot exceed day-22 exposure; the published
day-1 values are higher than day 22, which no linear model reproduces, and the
day-1 rows are shown for completeness.

```{r pk-sim}
mod_final <- readModelDb("Cerou_2024_amcenestrant")
ref_cov <- data.frame(
  MET_GE2 = 1, MET_GE3 = 1, LMET = 0, PREMENOPAUSAL = 0,
  AST = 28.4, AGE = 60
)
pk_obs <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 1, by = 1 / 96), seq(21, 22, by = 1 / 96))))
pk_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(
    id = 1L, time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = 400, cmt = "depot", ii = 1, addl = 21L
  ),
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = pk_obs, evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, cmt = "central")
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
  dplyr::bind_cols(typical_pk, ref_cov)

pk_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod_final), pk_events,
  returnType = "data.frame", method = "lsoda"
) |>
  # rxSolve() drops the id column for a single-subject solve
  dplyr::mutate(id = 1L, treatment = "400 mg QD")
```

```{r pknca}
conc <- pk_sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(id, treatment, time_h = time * 24, Cc = Cc * 1000) |> # ng/mL
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, time_h, .keep_all = TRUE)
dose <- data.frame(id = 1L, treatment = "400 mg QD", time_h = (0:21) * 24, amt = 400)

o_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time_h | treatment + id)
o_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose, amt ~ time_h | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 504), end = c(24, 528),
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cmin = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  day = c("Day 1", "Day 22")
)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose, intervals = intervals[, 1:6]))
nca_res <- as.data.frame(nca) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = ifelse(start == 0, "Day 1", "Day 22"))

# Tamura 2023 (AMEERA-2), 400 mg QD: Table 3 geometric means (tmax median);
# the day-22 trough is the arithmetic mean in the Results text (348 +/- 83.7).
reference <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("Day 1", "Day 22"),
  cmax = c(5500, 4880),
  tmax = c(2.90, 2.97),
  auclast = c(48500, 39800),
  cmin = c(NA, 348)
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = reference,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", tmax = "h", auclast = "h*ng/mL", cmin = "ng/mL")
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Illustrative typical PK against the AMEERA-2 NCA at 400 mg QD.")
```

The day-22 Cmax, tmax and AUCtau match by construction, and the day-22 trough
(about 390 ng/mL) sits between the AMEERA-2 (348 ng/mL) and AMEERA-1
(466 ng/mL) values.

```{r pk-gate}
d22 <- nca_res |>
  dplyr::filter(treatment == "Day 22") |>
  dplyr::select(PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
stopifnot(
  abs(d22$auclast / 39800 - 1) < 0.03,
  abs(d22$cmax / 4880 - 1) < 0.05,
  d22$cmin > 348, d22$cmin < 466
)
```

# Typical-patient tumor and PFS trajectories

```{r typical-helpers}
# One subject dosed 400 mg QD for `days`; observations every half day on the
# sensitive-cell state (TS, the hazard and survival are computed alongside).
make_events <- function(days, covs, obs_step = 0.5, id = 1L) {
  obs <- seq(0, days, by = obs_step)
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = id, time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = 400, cmt = "depot", ii = 1, addl = days - 1L),
    data.frame(id = id, time = obs, evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, cmt = "tumor_sensitive")
  ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    dplyr::bind_cols(typical_pk, covs[rep(1, length(obs) + 1), , drop = FALSE])
}
# `lsoda` is used throughout: the default `liblsoda` fails ("could not solve
# the system") on runs longer than about 250 days whose observation times
# coincide with the daily doses.
solve_typical <- function(model, events) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(model), events, returnType = "data.frame", method = "lsoda")
}
```

```{r typical-sim}
mod_dev <- readModelDb("Cerou_2024_amcenestrant_ameera12")
ref_cov_dev <- data.frame(MET_GE3 = 1, LMET = 0, LNMET = 0, PRIOR_CDK46I = 1, ALBR = 0.74, ALPR = 0.89)

typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  solve_typical(mod_final, make_events(350, ref_cov)) |> dplyr::mutate(model = "AMEERA-1-2-3 (final)"),
  solve_typical(mod_dev, make_events(350, ref_cov_dev)) |> dplyr::mutate(model = "AMEERA-1-2 (development)")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(week = time / 7)

onset <- typ |>
  dplyr::group_by(model) |>
  dplyr::arrange(time, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    sensitive_decline_week = week[which(diff(tumor_sensitive) < 0)[1]],
    ts_peak_week = week[which.max(TS * (week < 20))],
    ts_peak = max(TS[week < 20]),
    ts_nadir_week = week[which.min(TS)],
    ts_nadir = min(TS),
    pfs_week50 = surv[which.min(abs(week - 50))]
  )
knitr::kable(onset, digits = 2, caption = "Typical-patient landmarks at 400 mg QD (reference covariates).")
```

```{r typical-plot, fig.height = 6}
typ |>
  dplyr::select(week, model, `Tumor size (mm)` = TS, `PFS probability` = surv) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(week, model)) |>
  ggplot(aes(week, value, colour = model)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~name, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (weeks)", y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The paper states that for a typical patient on 400 mg QD "the delay to observe
the TS decrease was about 4.6 weeks" with the final model and "about 1.5 weeks"
with the development model. Reading "TS decrease" as the start of the decline of
the sensitive-cell population (the first moment the drug effect outweighs
proliferation), the final model reproduces the statement (row above); the
development model gives about 3.7 weeks, not 1.5. No parameter of the
development model can move that onset by a factor of 2.5 at a plausible
exposure (ke0 is fixed and the onset scales with the square root of the
exposure), so the 1.5-week figure is noted as not reproduced.

```{r onset-gate}
stopifnot(
  abs(onset$sensitive_decline_week[onset$model == "AMEERA-1-2-3 (final)"] - 4.6) < 1
)
```

# Replicating Figure 3: covariate effects in the final model

Figure 3 of Cerou 2024 shows the typical TS (panel a) and PFS (panel b) over 50
weeks at 400 mg QD when one covariate at a time moves away from the reference
(age 60 years, AST 28 IU/L, postmenopausal, metastases in three or more organs,
no liver metastasis). The table compares the packaged model with values read
from the figure by the maintainers (accuracy about +/- 1 mm and +/- 0.03).

```{r fig3-sim}
scenarios <- list(
  "Reference" = list(),
  "AGE 42 y" = list(AGE = 42),
  "AGE 79 y" = list(AGE = 79),
  "AST 17 IU/L" = list(AST = 17),
  "AST 88 IU/L" = list(AST = 88),
  "Pre/peri-menopausal" = list(PREMENOPAUSAL = 1),
  "NMET = 1" = list(MET_GE2 = 0, MET_GE3 = 0),
  "NMET = 2" = list(MET_GE2 = 1, MET_GE3 = 0),
  "Liver metastasis" = list(LMET = 1)
)
fig3 <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(scenarios), function(nm) {
  covs <- ref_cov
  for (v in names(scenarios[[nm]])) covs[[v]] <- scenarios[[nm]][[v]]
  solve_typical(mod_final, make_events(350, covs)) |> dplyr::mutate(scenario = nm)
})) |>
  dplyr::mutate(week = time / 7, scenario = factor(scenario, levels = names(scenarios)))

# Read from Figure 3 by the maintainers.
fig3_digitised <- data.frame(
  scenario = names(scenarios),
  ts0_fig = c(43.2, 43.2, 43.2, 43.2, 43.2, 60.6, 29.5, 29.0, 55.4),
  ts50_fig = c(36.8, 30.3, 41.1, 34.2, 46.7, 51.5, 25.1, 24.6, 63.5),
  pfs50_fig = c(0.35, 0.39, 0.33, 0.52, 0.05, 0.34, 0.36, 0.37, 0.04)
)
fig3_cmp <- fig3 |>
  dplyr::group_by(scenario) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    ts0 = TS[time == 0][1],
    ts50 = TS[which.min(abs(week - 50))],
    pfs50 = surv[which.min(abs(week - 50))]
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(scenario = as.character(scenario)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(fig3_digitised, by = "scenario")
fig3_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Scenario = scenario,
    "TS0 model (mm)" = ts0, "TS0 Fig 3" = ts0_fig,
    "TS wk 50 model (mm)" = ts50, "TS wk 50 Fig 3" = ts50_fig,
    "PFS wk 50 model" = pfs50, "PFS wk 50 Fig 3" = pfs50_fig
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Typical-patient TS and PFS by covariate (final model) against Figure 3.")
```

```{r fig3-plot, fig.height = 7}
fig3 |>
  dplyr::filter(week <= 50) |>
  dplyr::select(week, scenario, `Tumor size (mm)` = TS, `PFS probability` = surv) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(week, scenario)) |>
  ggplot(aes(week, value, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~name, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (weeks)", y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

Replicates Figure 3 of Cerou 2024. Baseline TS for every covariate level is
exact (it is closed form). Week-50 TS and PFS agree with the figure for every
covariate level. The intermediate shape differs: the published reference curve
peaks at about 44.3 mm near week 7 (reproduced) but reaches its nadir of about
32.5 mm near week 24, whereas the packaged model with the illustrative PK
reaches about 36 mm near week 39. Raising the exposure moves the peak earlier
and so cannot reproduce both landmarks; the authors' own PK input, which the
paper does not report, is the likely cause. The published PFS curves are also
flat for the first two weeks, which suggests they were drawn from simulated
event times rather than from the hazard directly.

```{r fig3-gate}
stopifnot(
  # Baseline TS is closed form: TS0 * exp(beta) for the covariate level.
  all(abs(fig3_cmp$ts0 / fig3_cmp$ts0_fig - 1) < 0.02),
  # Week-50 values: a sign or magnitude error in any covariate coefficient
  # moves these far outside the digitising accuracy.
  all(abs(fig3_cmp$ts50 / fig3_cmp$ts50_fig - 1) < 0.10),
  all(abs(fig3_cmp$pfs50 - fig3_cmp$pfs50_fig) < 0.06)
)
```

# Virtual-cohort simulation (compare with Figure 4)

Figure 4 shows the visual predictive check of the final model on all 214
patients. A virtual cohort of 200 patients on 400 mg QD is simulated with
covariates drawn to match Table 2 (all patients). Each simulated patient
progresses when the survival probability falls below a uniform random draw, and
TS is not counted after progression, as in the paper's VPC.

```{r vpc-cohort}
set.seed(20240601)
n_sub <- 200
nmet_draw <- sample(c(1, 2, 3), n_sub, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.2735, 0.2735, 0.453))
cohort <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  LMET = rbinom(n_sub, 1, 0.472),
  MET_GE2 = as.integer(nmet_draw >= 2),
  MET_GE3 = as.integer(nmet_draw >= 3),
  PREMENOPAUSAL = 0,
  AGE = pmin(pmax(round(rnorm(n_sub, 60, 11)), 29), 88),
  AST = pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(n_sub, log(28.4), 0.45)), 7), 180)
)
vpc_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n_sub), function(i) {
  make_events(630, cohort[i, -1, drop = FALSE], obs_step = 7, id = i)
}))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20240601)
vpc <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_final, vpc_events, returnType = "data.frame", method = "lsoda")
stopifnot(all(is.finite(vpc$surv)))

u <- data.frame(id = seq_len(n_sub), u = runif(n_sub))
vpc <- vpc |>
  dplyr::left_join(u, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::mutate(progressed = cumsum(surv < u) > 0) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::mutate(week = time / 7)
```

```{r vpc-plot, fig.height = 6}
ts_pct <- vpc |>
  dplyr::filter(!progressed) |>
  dplyr::group_by(week) |>
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::n() >= 10) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), p50 = quantile(sim, 0.5), p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
pfs <- vpc |>
  dplyr::group_by(week) |>
  dplyr::summarise(pfs = mean(surv), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(ts_pct, aes(week)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50)) +
  labs(x = "Time (weeks)", y = "Tumor size (mm)",
       title = "Simulated TS before progression: median and 5th-95th percentiles") +
  theme_bw()
ggplot(pfs, aes(week, pfs)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Time (weeks)", y = "Progression-free probability",
       title = "Simulated PFS (mean survival probability)") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r vpc-summary}
pfs_landmarks <- data.frame(
  week = c(12, 20, 40, 80),
  simulated = sapply(c(12, 20, 40, 80), function(w) pfs$pfs[which.min(abs(pfs$week - w))]),
  figure4_km = c(0.50, 0.40, 0.27, 0.12)
)
knitr::kable(pfs_landmarks, digits = 2,
             caption = "Simulated PFS against the Figure 4 Kaplan-Meier estimate (read by the maintainers).")
ts_landmarks <- ts_pct |> dplyr::filter(week %in% c(0, 12, 24, 40))
knitr::kable(ts_landmarks, digits = 1, caption = "Simulated TS percentiles before progression.")
```

Replicates Figure 4 of Cerou 2024 qualitatively. The observed median TS in
Figure 4 starts near 42 mm and settles around 30-35 mm, and the 95th percentile
starts above 100 mm; the simulated cohort has the same shape. The simulated PFS
curve follows the Kaplan-Meier estimate. Differences come from the virtual
cohort (no PK variability, all patients postmenopausal, covariate distributions
approximated from Table 2 medians and ranges) and from the interval-censored
visit schedule of the trials, which this continuous-time simulation does not
reproduce.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **PK input.** The authors' population PK model is unpublished; the packaged
  models take the per-subject PK parameters as covariate columns, as the
  Monolix model did. The PK values used in this article were built by the
  maintainers from the published AMEERA-1 and AMEERA-2 noncompartmental results
  and carry no between-subject variability.
* **Omega scale.** Table 3 labels the random-effect magnitudes "coefficient of
  variation" but prints Monolix standard deviations multiplied by 100: Table S2
  prints the same quantities as SDs (0.56, 1.28, 0.92, 2.28 for the TGI-only
  calibrated model), and a coefficient of variation is not defined for the
  logit-normal RE. The models use variance = (printed value / 100)^2.
* **pR distribution.** Methods state log-normal random effects for every
  parameter except RE. With a log-normal pR of 0.66 and SD 0.84, about 31% of
  patients would have pR above 1 and a negative sensitive-cell population. The
  models put pR on the logit scale, which keeps it in (0, 1).
* **Covariate centering.** Continuous covariates enter as log(value / median).
  AST is centred on the raw calibration-set median of 28.4 IU/L (Table 2); the
  paper uses AST normalised to the upper limit of normal, which is the same
  thing when all laboratories share an upper limit. Figure 3 labels the AST
  levels in IU/L (17, 28, 88), which supports this reading. For the development
  model the normalised albumin and alkaline phosphatase medians are not in the
  paper: 0.74 (albumin) and 0.89 (alkaline phosphatase) come from the per-study
  medians in the authors' PAGE 2022 poster on the same 75 patients. Raw alkaline
  phosphatase cannot be used instead: AMEERA-2 used a different upper limit.
* **NMET categories.** The final model's NMET = 1 and NMET = 2 indicators
  (reference three or more organs) are formed from `MET_GE2` and `MET_GE3`; a
  patient with no metastatic organ falls in the NMET = 1 group.
* **Treatment start.** Monolix used a regressor `Tstart` for the start of the
  PFS clock. The packaged models start both the hazard and the drug at time 0;
  shift the dosing if the clock starts earlier.
* **Third effect compartment.** The Monolix file declares a third effect
  compartment `C3` that drives nothing; it is omitted.
* **Hazard numerics.** The Weibull term uses `t + 1e-6` days so that the
  shape below 1 does not give an infinite hazard at time 0, and the link
  exponent is capped at 50 because an ODE keeps integrating after a simulated
  progression; at the cap the hazard exceeds 1e18 per day and survival is
  already zero.
* **Development-model onset.** The development model does not reproduce the
  stated 1.5-week delay to tumor decrease (3.7 weeks with these PK values).
* **Figure 2 (external evaluation on AMEERA-3)** is not replicated: AMEERA-3
  albumin, alkaline phosphatase and lymph-node-metastasis distributions are not
  reported.
